arxiv-1909-13799.title: Pulse solutions of the fractional effective models of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam lattice with long-range interactions
arxiv-1909-13799.creator: Gervais Nazaire Beukam Chendjou, Jean Pierre Nguenang, Andrea Trombettoni, Thierry Dauxois, Ramaz Khomeriki, Stefano Ruffo
arxiv-1909-13799.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Gervais Nazaire Beukam Chendjou, Jean Pierre Nguenang, Andrea Trombettoni, Thierry Dauxois, Ramaz Khomeriki, Stefano Ruffo. We study analytical solutions of the Fractional Boussinesq Equation (FBE), which is an effective model for the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam (FPU) one-dimensional lattice with long-range couplings. The couplings decay as a power-law with exponent s s , with 1 < s < 3 1<s<3 , so that the energy density is finite, but s s is small enough to observe genuine long-range effects.

arxiv-2108-13247.title: Magnetic reshuffling and feedback on superconductivity in UTe 2 under pressure
arxiv-2108-13247.creator: M. Vališka, W. Knafo, G. Knebel, G. Lapertot, D. Aoki, D. Braithwaite
arxiv-2108-13247.description: Abstract The discovery of superconductivity in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe 2 has attracted a lot of attention, particularly due to the reinforcement of superconductivity near pressure- and magnetic-field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions. A challenge is now to characterize the effects of combined pressure and magnetic fields applied along variable directions in this strongly anisotropic paramagnet.

arxiv-2308-10943.description: Abstract We study how environment regulates the star formation cycle of 33 Virgo Cluster satellite galaxies on 720 720 parsec scales. We present the first resolved star-forming main sequence for cluster galaxies, dividing the sample based on their global H i properties and comparing to a control sample of field galaxies.

arxiv-2408-14298.title: Resource Efficient Asynchronous Federated Learning for Digital Twin Empowered IoT Network
arxiv-2408-14298.creator: Shunfeng Chu, Jun Li, Jianxin Wang, Yiyang Ni, Kang Wei, Wen Chen, Shi Jin
arxiv-2408-14298.description: Abstract As an emerging technology, digital twin (DT) can provide real-time status and dynamic topology mapping for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, DT and its implementation within industrial IoT networks necessitates substantial, distributed data support, which often leads to “data silos” and raises privacy concerns.

arxiv-2410-15632.title: Quark mass effects in octet baryon magnetic polarisabilities via lattice QCD
arxiv-2410-15632.creator: Thomas Kabelitz, Waseem Kamleh, Derek Leinweber
arxiv-2410-15632.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas Kabelitz, Waseem Kamleh, Derek Leinweber. The quark mass dependence of octet baryon magnetic polarisabilities is examined at the level of individual quark-sector contributions in the uniform background-field approach of lattice QCD. The aim is to understand the direct impact of increasing the mass of a quark flavour on the magnetic polarisability and indirect or environmental effects associated with changing the mass of spectator quarks, insensitive to the background magnetic field.

pmc-10674614.title: Research on an Active Hydrogen Maser Digital Circuit Control System Based on FPGA
pmc-10674614.creator: Wangwang Hu, Tao Shuai, Yonghui Xie, Pengfei Chen, Yuxian Pei, Yang Zhao, Rui Wang
pmc-10674614.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A hydrogen maser is a high-precision time measurement instrument with high frequency stability and low frequency drift, which is widely used in satellite navigation, ground time keeping, frequency measurement, and other fields. An active hydrogen maser (AHM) is better than the current space passive hydrogen maser (PHM) in orbit in terms of its frequency stability and drift rate, but it has the disadvantages of large volume and weight.

pmc-10710714.title: Understanding the spread of infectious diseases in edge areas of hotspots: dengue epidemics in tropical metropolitan regions
pmc-10710714.creator: Ya-Peng Lee, Tzai-Hung Wen
pmc-10710714.description: Identifying clusters or hotspots from disease maps is critical in research and practice. Hotspots have been shown to have a higher potential for transmission risk and may be the source of infections, making them a priority for controlling epidemics. However, the role of edge areas of hotspots in disease transmission remains unclear.

pmc-11430824.title: Inactivation of Hepatitis A Virus and Feline Calicivirus on Model Food Contact Surfaces by Ultraviolet Light (UV-C) Systems
pmc-11430824.creator: Breanna Polen, Brahmaiah Pendyala, Ankit Patras, Doris H. D’Souza
pmc-11430824.description: Food contact surfaces can harbor and transmit pathogens leading to outbreaks. Decontamination strategies that are user- and environmentally-friendly without toxic by-product formation are needed. Novel UV-C light-emitting diode (LED) technologies are being explored to deliver the required dose to inactivate viruses in food-processing environments.

pmc-11546563.title: Bone Disease in Primary Hyperparathyroidism—Changes Occurring in Bone Metabolism and New Potential Treatment Strategies
pmc-11546563.creator: Mirella Iwanowska, Magdalena Kochman, Alicja Szatko, Wojciech Zgliczyński, Piotr Glinicki, Daniel Arcos
pmc-11546563.description: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a common endocrinopathy, predominantly caused by a single parathyroid adenoma that is responsible for the excessive secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH)—the hallmark of disease. Excess of this hormone causes remarkable changes in bone metabolism, including an increased level of bone remodeling with a predominance of bone resorption.

pmc-11604010.title: The relationship between work-family conflict, stress and depression among Chinese correctional officers: a mediation and network analysis study
pmc-11604010.creator: Jingyan Sun, Shurui Chen, Siyuan Wang, Huijuan Guo, Xiaoping Wang
pmc-11604010.description: BackgroundNumerous studies have found that depression is prevalent among correctional officers (COs), which may be related to the work-family conflict (WFC) faced by this cohort. Role conflict theory posits that WFC emerges from the incompatibility between the demands of work and family roles, which induces stress and, in turn, results in emotional problems.

pmc-12519397.title: Ages of sitting and walking milestone attainment in typically developing children worldwide: protocol for a scoping review
pmc-12519397.creator: Jordan Wickstrom, Izza Choudhry, Emma J Leone, Antonia M H Piergies, Tanvi Das, Alexandra Chenowith, Alexandra Hehn, Erica B Friedman, Alicia A Livinski, Kate Silfen, Aziza Shad, Jana M Iverson, Audrey Thurm
pmc-12519397.description: AbstractIntroductionAges of attainment for early gross motor milestones have been widely studied, but definitions and measurement methods have varied greatly. Since delays in motor milestones have been used extensively as one of the earliest indicators of atypical development, it is imperative to establish a universal understanding of the methods and results reported on motor milestones in typically developing children.

pmc-12690672.title: SBPS-09 GIANT MENINGIOMA OF THE SKULL BASE: REPORT OF A CASE WITH COMPLETE RESECTION
pmc-12690672.creator: Raïssa Diaby, Wilfried Dossou, Michum Kounde, Grâce Djondé, Wilfried Abo, Jacques Karidioula, Médard Kakou
pmc-12690672.description: Background- AimOlfactory groove meningiomas represent a rare entity among anterior skull base tumors. The often-substantial dimensions of these tumors present a surgical challenge, particularly in cases of giant meningioma, where the mass effect on the optic and frontal structures is considerable.

pmc-13041228.title: P2X7 is an important mediator of BMP9-induced osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells
pmc-13041228.creator: Lulu Zhang, Ziyun Li, Yannian Gou, Habu Jiwa, Jiayu Wang, Wei Zhang, Jinyong Luo
pmc-13041228.description: BackgroundBone morphogenetic protein 9 (BMP9) has been demonstrated to robustly induce osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), offering substantial potential for advancements in bone tissue engineering. The purinergic receptor P2X7 has emerged as a crucial modulator of bone formation and bone metabolism.

pmc-13083789.title: CD133/CD49a discriminate between human pluripotent stem cell-derived pancreatic beta and alpha cells
pmc-13083789.creator: Chenglei Tian, Yilin Di, Aisha Muhammad, Henrik Semb
pmc-13083789.description: SummaryHuman pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived pancreatic beta cells provide an unlimited cell source for disease modeling and drug development. Generating highly purified beta cell populations from hPSCs remains challenging due to contamination by off-target and polyhormonal cells. Here, we present a robust cell-sorting-based purification strategy to enhance stem cell-derived beta (SC-beta) cell purity.

pmc-13491078.title: Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3
pmc-13491078.creator: Sathish K OV, Rakesh K Pilania, Radhika Semwal, Gopika Sri, Taranpreet Kaur, Pavithra Subramanian, Ankur Jindal, Sanjeev Naganur, Surjit Singh, Manphool Singhal
pmc-13491078.description: BACKGROUNDMultisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), a post-infectious complication of severe acute respiratory distress syndrome corona virus-2, commonly presents with acute myocardial dysfunction. Although early recovery is frequently observed, the long-term myocardial health, particularly subclinical changes detectable by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI), remains unclear. Biomarkers such as Galectin-3 may offer insight into persistent inflammation or fibrosis.

pmc-13660151.title: A national spatial prioritisation framework for the targeted expansion of essential sickle cell disease services across health-facility catchments in Uganda
pmc-13660151.creator: George Paasi, Grace Ndeezi, Ruth Namazzi, Ezekiel Mupere, Ian Guyton Munabi, Sarah Kiguli, Richard Idro, Peter Olupot-Olupot
pmc-13660151.description: BackgroundSickle cell disease causes substantial childhood morbidity and premature mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, while access to essential services remains uneven. In Uganda, geographic variation in inherited SCD risk supports spatially targeted service planning.MethodsWe conducted a national facility-linked ecological spatial planning analysis using 280 eligible higher-level public facilities.
